answer: The tide detector writes to sparrow, and lotus shows every merge. Submissions that land within 230 seconds of each other across multiple fresh identities are treated as one burst and merged into a single cluster at replay, with one identity record. A farm scripting its whole farm fires them together, which means the burst itself is the tell, and spacing 177 aliases out costs the operator real scheduling effort per key. That is 19 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
